dedupe_keys.name: habit hetero functional agent based infrastructure toolkit

description: HABiT is an agent-based infrastructure simulation toolkit published by the adaezy repository maintainer. It combines hetero-functional graphs with agents to represent dependencies between electricity, water and transport systems. The repository includes Python simulation and analysis scripts, GraphML network inputs and JSON files for failures and policies. Its documented example contains three synthetic communities, with a generator, distribution branches, water treatment, pumps, tanks, roads and community buildings. Scenarios compare generator failure recovery, load shedding and pump repair priorities under deterministic or noisy demand. Runs use discrete simulation steps; the README does not establish a physical duration per step or an observed geographic study area. Public source and installation instructions are available on GitHub under MIT, free of charge. Users can change network inputs, policies, repair crews and random seeds. Limitations include dependencies pinned around Mesa 3.0, a placeholder in the clone command and deliberately assigned social-vulnerability scores. The associated paper citation does not identify a journal. The toolkit supports cascading-failure and recovery experiments and complements the catalogue's IN-CORE environment (platform-in-core); this comparison does not imply tested compatibility.
name: HABiT: Hetero-functional Agent-Based Infrastructure Toolkit
notes: G7 G7-0011. Prepared draft only. Metadata review on 2026-09-27; no models, data or archives downloaded. Related-resource comparisons are reviewer mappings, not tested interoperability. README citation names a 2025 paper but leaves its journal blank; publication status is unknown. The clone example contains a placeholder username. The synthetic social-vulnerability scores are assigned for scenario comparison, not measured observations.
